summary: Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2012).
Hiroyuki Kato (1836–1916) worked in philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Bansho Shirabesho (~1860–1862), Kaisei School (~1863–1869), and the University of Tokyo (~1877–1893).
Hisanosuke Izui (1905–1983) was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928). He later held a post at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–1978).

Hisao Inagaki (1929–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and SOAS University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki (1918–1996) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (~1962–1973), Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1973–1982), and Komazawa University (~1982–1993).

Hisao Takahashi (born 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University (~1970–1975) under Ryukai Mano and held positions there as assistant (attested 1977–1982), lecturer (attested 1995), and professor (~1996–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and served as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato (1913–2008) studied at Kyoto University (~1935–1938) and worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University, and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1977–1984).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna (-2011) under Helmut Krasser, later serving as lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).

Hisatake Kato (1937–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Yamagata University, Tohoku University, Tottori University of Environmental Studies, and University of Human Arts and Sciences.

Hisayoshi Miyamoto (born 1948) works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, and studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. Attested in 2026, he is a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held posts at Koyasan University as lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Kato (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University (all attested 1992), as well as Osaka University (attested 2016).

Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who earned his MA at the University of Rangoon and his doctorate at SOAS. He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese there from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Washington (-1994) under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada and served as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1959–1963) and was a disciple of Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hoju (born 1980) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University (~1999–2003) and KU Leuven (~2005–2007), and taught Kyokuga Saeki.
Hoju Shioda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Minobusan University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (both attested 2026).

Hojun Nagasaki (born 1934) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1964–1967), was professor emeritus at Otani University (~1970–1999), and served as president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies (1998).
